$comment: Gate B DRAFT rule object for RF-REHAB-006 — pending, NON-EXECUTABLE. Authored only from RF Clinical Rule Specification v1.2 §10.9 and the RF-REHAB-006 inventory entry. Architecture-source rule: evidence_claim_ids intentionally empty per v1.2 §4.3. Expresses concurrent-injury constraint and compatible-plan gating STRUCTURE only: when one or more secondary/contributing/concurrent/referred/compensatory/chronic conditions are active, compose one programme under the MOST RESTRICTIVE active contraindication, avoiding incompatible loading and duplicate workload while preserving safe unaffected training. If no plan satisfies every active contraindication, set terminal REHAB_BLOCKED, withhold the plan, and refer. No condition may be silently ignored. No dosage, exercise selection, complete RF or combined plan, RTT, or RTS logic; compatibility alone is not progression or readiness; safety precedence preserved; does not bypass RF-REHAB-001/002/003/004/005 or override RF-SAF-006/RF-DX-008/RF-SEV-004/RF-SEV-005. Not approved. Not wired into any runtime.
rule_title: Concurrent injury constraints govern or block the plan

input_contract.$comment: Activation and compatibility-check domains taken verbatim-in-meaning from v1.2 §10.9. Concurrent-injury constraints are required inputs; unknown external concurrent-injury restrictions remain unknown and trigger governed missing-data behaviour, never silent clearance.

decision_contract.$comment: Concurrent-injury compatibility / blocking structure only. Concurrent injuries govern; compose one programme under the most restrictive active contraindication; if no compatible plan exists, terminal REHAB_BLOCKED, withhold, and refer. No condition silently ignored. No dosage, exercise selection, complete RF or combined plan, RTT, or RTS; compatibility alone is not progression or readiness. Safety precedence preserved.

notes: Architecture normative source; MUST; permitted_use logic_with_uncertainty. Architecture refs preserved per source: V3.1-11 (concurrent & secondary injuries) and V3.1-15.2 (concurrent-injury role taxonomy / reconciliation). No evidence_claim_ids are cited (legitimately empty per v1.2 §4.3 — architecture rules need not invent evidence claims; [] means 'none required', not 'missing'). Per §10.9 activation: one or more secondary, contributing, concurrent, referred, compensatory, or chronic conditions are active. Per §10.9 decision preserved exactly: compose one programme under the most restrictive active contraindication; avoid incompatible loading and duplicate workload while preserving safe unaffected training. Per §10.9 conflict behaviour preserved exactly: if no plan satisfies every active contraindication, set terminal REHAB_BLOCKED, withhold the plan, and refer; no condition may be silently ignored. Safety-state choice (read §10.9 exactly): §10.9 EXPLICITLY assigns terminal REHAB_BLOCKED for the no-compatible-plan case, so safety_state_output is REHAB_BLOCKED with blocked_targets ['rehab'] (V3.1 §21 terminal REHAB_BLOCKED, withhold and refer; consistent with RF-SAF-006). This was taken directly from the source, not inferred by analogy; the compatible-route branch (compose under the most restrictive contraindication) is represented as structure in decision_contract and is never a complete plan. The rule does not prioritize RF rehab over a more restrictive concurrent-injury constraint, never silently ignores or assumes concurrent injuries/restrictions/other plans compatible, and treats unknown compatibility/restrictions/capacity impact as governed missing-data rather than clearance. It creates no dosage, selects no exercises or complete exercise plan, generates no complete RF or combined rehab plan, and produces no return-to-training or return-to-sport decision; compatibility alone is not progression and not readiness. It does not bypass RF-REHAB-001/002/003/004/005 and does not override RF-SAF-006, RF-DX-008, RF-SEV-004, or RF-SEV-005; uncertainty is preserved when concurrent-injury, external-restriction, capacity, monitoring, schedule, or compatibility data are incomplete. Rehabilitation concurrent-injury governing/blocking rule. No rehab engine is authored here (deferred to the later rehab selection and planning objects). Draft — approval_status remains pending.
